transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in because I’ve been really stuck on this idea that certain people around the arts and finance circles here in Cincinnati are kind of... tracking who I meet with, which clients I’m seeing. It feels like they send little signals through things like event invitations, panel topics, even who ends up sitting near me at events.

I know part of me can say maybe it’s all coincidence, but I can’t really let it go, and it’s been bothering me enough that I thought I should talk to someone.
Besides these suspicions about being tracked, have you ever heard voices or sounds that others couldn't hear, or seen things that weren't really there?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t heard voices or seen things that other people couldn’t see. It’s more about how I interpret certain situations or patterns, I guess.
How long have you been having these thoughts about being tracked—did they start suddenly at some point, or is this a way of thinking about people that's been part of your personality for many years?

It’s been about two months, I’d say. It didn’t feel like it was always part of how I think about people. It kind of built up over that time, but the tracking and signals idea has really been there for around two months.
During these past two months, have you also noticed changes in your mood—like feeling unusually sad, hopeless, or on the other hand, unusually energetic, elated, or irritable—that lasted for a while?
I’m not really sure. I wouldn’t say I’ve felt unusually happy or energized. Maybe more stressed or on edge because of the situation, but I haven’t noticed a big mood swing or anything like that.
Have you had any recent medical illnesses, head injuries, or been using any drugs, alcohol, or new medications around the time these suspicions started?

Not that I can think of. I haven’t had any head injury or anything like that. I’m not aware of any medical illness around then, and I haven’t started any new medication. I don’t really use drugs, and alcohol hasn’t been anything out of the ordinary.

Have you noticed any changes in how you organize your thoughts or speech, or has anyone commented that your speech seems disorganized or hard to follow? Also, have you lost interest in activities, or noticed a decrease in your motivation or ability to show emotion?

My thoughts and speech feel mostly organized, I think. I haven’t had anyone tell me I’m hard to follow.

But motivation, yeah… that’s been off. I still get my work done, but it’s more in pieces, and I’ll leave client follow-ups sitting longer than I should. I don’t really have the same spark. I’ve been skipping jazz nights and pickup basketball, and I don’t feel much about missing them. And when friends ask what’s going on, I just give short answers because talking feels like more effort than it should.
You mentioned your motivation and interest in things like jazz nights and basketball have dropped off—about how long has that been going on?

It’s been a while… I’d say it’s been building since that arts nonprofit recognition thing, a little over two years ago. It wasn’t all at once, but since then I’ve noticed I just haven’t been as interested or motivated.

Over these past two years, has this drop in motivation and interest actually affected your job performance or your relationships in a noticeable way, or have you still been able to keep things running fairly normally?

I’ve still been able to keep things going, but not like before. I’m working, but my practice has gotten smaller. I miss follow-ups more than I used to, and I avoid some public panels or events now. I just don’t keep up the same level of client contact I used to, so yeah, it has affected work in a noticeable way.

It’s mostly work and social stuff, I think. I still take care of myself at home, but I just don’t have the same drive. Like I’ll do things in pieces, put off client follow-ups, skip jazz or basketball, and when friends reach out I keep it short because talking feels like effort. It’s not like everything has fallen apart, but I’m definitely more withdrawn than I used to be.
Have you or people close to you noticed that your facial expressions or emotional reactions seem more flat or muted lately, compared to how you used to show emotion?

Yeah… maybe a little. I still react to things, but I don’t feel like I have the same spark as before. I get my work done, kind of in pieces, but I’ll let follow-ups sit there, skip jazz nights or basketball, and not feel much about it. And when friends ask what’s going on, I usually just give short answers because talking feels like more effort than it should.
